items.title: Santo Pecora Interview, 1972-11-09
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Somebody could play Rattie on trumpet.

ctx.x: Yeah, you knew him. All right. Johnny Bystorfer got sick for about three weeks. So Tommy takes the trumpet and plays the big show. I can believe it. A beautiful trumpet. Oh man. I said, how in the hell can you play trumpet and take the trumpet? He used to like the trombones. He wanted to play trombone. But he used to play that show, cut that show like that.
He sounded like Joe Olive on trumpet to me. Some of the records. He sounded like Joe Olive on trumpet. No. Somebody could play Rattie on trumpet.

No, he sounded like Harry James or Spivak or something like that. Oh, he had a beautiful tone. Everything, numb pressure and all that. Tommy played beautiful. Look at it. But he had to get on that trombone. But him and I, and he used to practice in the hotel room. Gee, nine o'clock in the morning. We'd go home about four o'clock in the morning. Get up at nine o'clock and practice with records and all that stuff. We got to be pretty good friends. Well, you know who bought Jack Teagarden first trombone? Me. You…
